## 1. Feature Correctness

## 2. Code Quality and Architecture

Evaluate:
- Separation of concerns.
- Consistency with existing cal.diy architecture.
- Appropriate reuse of existing components, services, and repositories.

## 3. Security and Authorization

Pay particular attention to:
- Whether only authorized hosts can retrieve and manage recurring occurrences.
- Whether checking access to one booking is sufficient to return the entire recurring series.
- Whether organizers can change between occurrences.
- Whether manipulating bookingId or recurringEventId could expose unauthorized information.
- Whether invalid confirmation or rejection requests are rejected server-side.
- Whether simultaneous requests could cause invalid booking status transitions.

Distinguish actual vulnerabilities from theoretical possibilities.

## 4. Functional Behavior and Regression Risks

Verify the following scenarios:

- Confirming one occurrence does not affect other occurrences.
- Rejecting one occurrence preserves the other bookings.
- Rejection reasons are correctly saved.
- Previously confirmed, rejected, cancelled, or past bookings cannot be incorrectly modified.
- Confirm all and Reject all still function correctly.
- Individual actions refresh the dialog, booking dashboard, and pending booking count.
- Confirming individual occurrences before selecting Confirm all does not create duplicate calendar events.
- Existing non-recurring booking behavior remains correct.
- Email confirmation links and API v2 callers continue to work as intended.
- Payment and refund behavior does not introduce new inconsistencies.
- Time zones and exact time boundaries are handled correctly.

Determine whether any identified regression was introduced by this PR or existed previously.

## 5. Testing Quality

- Whether excessive mocking hides implementation defects.
- Whether important integration or regression tests are missing.
- Whether skipped existing tests reduce confidence in the implementation.

This repo runs Vitest 4.1, which ignores `vitest.workspace.ts`. Every test runs under the root `vitest.config.mts`, whose only setup file is `packages/testing/src/setupVitest.ts`. That file provides the jest-dom matchers and a ResizeObserver polyfill. The per-project setups named in the workspace file, such as `packages/ui/components/test-setup.tsx` with its next/navigation, useLocale and useIsPlatform mocks, never run.

**Why:** anything that renders `@calcom/features/components/controlled-dialog` throws "invariant expected app router to be mounted" unless the test file mocks `next/navigation`'s `useRouter` itself. `EditLocationDialog.test.tsx` and `RescheduleDialog.test.tsx` both do this.

**How to apply:**
- When writing an `apps/web` component test, mock `next/navigation` (`useRouter`) and `@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale` in the test file.
- Run a single file with `yarn test <path>`. The script sets TZ=UTC, so the command also works in PowerShell.
- To type-check one test file with a temporary tsconfig placed outside the repo, set `typeRoots` to the repo's `node_modules/@types`. Otherwise `@types/jest` and `@types/testing-library__jest-dom` go missing and you get false errors.

Type checking on Julissa's Windows machine:
- `yarn type-check:ci --force` fails there with `spawn tsc ENOENT`. The `tsc-absolute` wrapper can't launch tsc on Windows, so this is a tooling problem, not a code problem.
- That run also re-formats `packages/prisma/schema.prisma` to LF line endings, a change with no content difference. Undo it with `git restore`.
- Instead, type-check the web app with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=12288 npx tsc --noEmit --pretty false -p apps/web/tsconfig.json` (~72s, the same heap CI uses).

Stale tRPC types (verified 2026-11-12):
- `apps/web` type checking reads `packages/trpc/types/`. That folder is gitignored build output, and Julissa's copy dates from 2026-10-08.
- Since #122, the stale copy causes `BookerWebWrapper.tsx:230 bookingPageColors` TS2322. Clean team/main shows the same error until the types are rebuilt; after a rebuild it type-checks with 0 errors.
- Fix: run `yarn prisma generate`, then `cd packages/trpc && yarn build`.
- To type-check a clean commit in a scratch clone, **copy** the ignored artifacts into it (prisma generated/enums/zod, trpc/types, platform dists, ui/svg-icons). If you junction them instead, TS loads two copies of each package and reports spurious PrismaClient errors.

Running a teammate's PR tests without touching Julissa's checkout (worked 2026-10-29 for PR #120):
- In the scratchpad, `git clone --shared --no-checkout` her repo. Fetch `pull/<n>/head` from GitHub into the clone and check it out with `core.longpaths=true`.
- Make `<clone>/node_modules` a real directory of junctions to her installed entries. Point the `@calcom/*` packages the PR changes at the clone. Point every other `@calcom/*` at her install, because a bare checkout lacks generated files such as `@calcom/prisma/enums`.
- From the clone, run `TZ=UTC node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run <files>` without going through yarn.
- Afterwards, remove the junctions with non-recursive `rmdir`. Windows PowerShell 5.1 `Remove-Item -Recurse` can follow junctions and delete their targets.
- `vitest.config.mts` has no `@components/*` alias, so the real `apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal` can't load in tests. A review-only config that adds the alias works. The render also needs Radix `TooltipProvider`, because PasswordField uses a tooltip.

Local database facts, verified 2026-10-29:
- Julissa's dev DB runs in docker container `prisma-postgres-1` (postgres:18) and is reached at `localhost:5450/calendso` via `.env`. `packages/prisma/.env` is a symlink to the root `.env`.
- Running the Prisma CLI from the repo root fails with "conflict between env vars in .env and packages\prisma\.env", so run it from `packages/prisma`.
- An inline `DATABASE_URL`/`DATABASE_DIRECT_URL` overrides `.env`. `migrate status` prints a `Datasource … at host:port` line, which is the safe pre-flight check.
- `@calcom/prisma`'s `build` script (`auto-migrations.ts`) runs `migrate deploy` against the `.env` DB unless `SKIP_DB_MIGRATIONS=1`. So `yarn build` migrates the dev DB. `type-check:ci` only runs post-install, so it doesn't.
- Avoid `db-migrate` (migrate dev), `db-reset`, `db-nuke` and `dx` against the dev DB.

**Biome on Windows (verified 2026-11-19):**
- `biome.json` sets `lineEnding: "lf"`, but Julissa has `core.autocrlf=true`. So every modified file shows one extra `format` error locally even when the content is fine.
- To judge real new diagnostics, compare `tr -d '\r'` copies placed next to the originals (same folder, so the same Biome config applies) against `git show team/main:<file>` copies.
- Never run `biome check --write` on whole existing files. It reformats unrelated lines.

Do not run git commands that create commits (`git commit`, `git cherry-pick`, `git rebase`, etc.) on this user's behalf, even when earlier in the same session the user asked for "changes" to be made or seemed to authorize it generally. Edit files, explain what needs to happen and why, and stage changes if asked, but leave the actual commit-creating step to the user.

**Why:** In a debugging/restart session on [[cal-diy-issue-11-reschedule-reason]], the user explicitly said "don't commit nothing i will do that you are here for guide" after noticing the assistant had made several commits (including a `git cherry-pick`, which auto-creates a commit) without a clear enough check-in first.

**How to apply:** When a fix or rebuild step is ready, describe the diff and let the user commit it. If a git operation is unavoidable and inherently commit-creating (e.g. cherry-pick to move a specific commit onto a new branch), ask first and be explicit that it will create a commit. This applies specifically to this user/repo; general commit-permission norms elsewhere still apply as usual.

The draft verdict is Request Changes, with scores Correctness 6 / Tests 6 / Quality 7 / Docs 7 / AI transparency 6 / Overall 6. Nothing has been posted. She is verifying the findings before she writes the review.

Key findings:
- **Confirmed bug.** `RequiredTwoFactorSetupModal` latches open from its first render. A second tab therefore stays on an undismissable modal after setup finishes in another tab. Setup then returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`, which the modal shows as "something went wrong". A probe test against the real modal reproduced this.
- **Test gap.** No test covers AC2 (no Cancel, Escape ignored), because both component tests mock `EnableTwoFactorModal`. When I mutated it to show Cancel and drop the notice, all 64 PR tests still passed.
- **Minor issues:**
  - The password step briefly reappears while `update()` is pending.
  - The jwt update branch calls `findById`, which fetches far more than it needs.
  - The PR reads the flag through a second path, separate from #111's `isTwoFactorRequiredSiteWide`.
  - It includes an unrelated #111 diagram file.
  - It exceeds the repo's PR size guideline.
- **Spec deviation.** The PR recomputes the flag on every session fetch, so already-logged-in users get the modal before their next login. #112 lists that as out of scope.
- **Client-only enforcement.** The PR description says `getServerSession` recalculates the flag. It doesn't.

**Why:** if Julissa comes back to post the review or follow up, start from here instead of re-reviewing from scratch.
**How to apply:** check PR #120 for new commits before reusing any finding. The PR adds `packages/features/auth/lib/requiresTwoFactorSetup.ts`, which [[issue-67-admin-2fa]] could reuse for its per-request admin checks. {"author":{"id":"U_kgDOBhId4A","is_bot":false,"login":"julissaehp","name":""},"body":"### User Story\n\nAs a host managing recurring bookings, I want to confirm or reject individual occurrences so that I can handle scheduling conflicts without affecting the entire recurring series.\n\n### User Scenario\n\nA host receives a request for 10 recurring Tennis classes scheduled every two weeks. The host is available for nine of the dates but has a scheduling conflict on one.\n\nCurrently, the Bookings dashboard displays \"Confirm all\" and \"Reject all\" for recurring bookings. Although each occurrence has its own booking status, the host cannot easily confirm or reject individual dates through the default interface.\n\nThe host should be able to open a \"Manage occurrences\" dialog, review each scheduled date, and confirm or reject specific occurrences while leaving the remaining bookings unchanged.\n\n### Current Behavior\n\nManual testing and code investigation identified the following:\n\n1. The Unconfirmed and Recurring tabs display bulk confirmation actions.\n2. Clicking the recurring booking link displays the occurrence dates without individual confirmation controls.\n3. The three-dot menu does not provide individual confirmation or rejection options.\n4. The default Bookings dashboard collapses recurring bookings into one representative row.\n5. The backend already supports individual confirmation and rejection when `recurringEventId` is omitted from the confirmation request.\n\n**Technical evidence:**\n\n- `apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useBookingListData.ts` — collapses recurring series into a single row.\n- `apps/web/components/booking/hooks/useBookingConfirmation.tsx` — determines whether a confirmation request applies to one booking or the recurring series.\n- `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts` — handles confirmation and rejection requests.\n- `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleConfirmation.ts` — supports updating an individual booking.\n- `apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx` — renders recurring booking actions and the occurrence-date tooltip.\n\n### Expected Behavior\n\nHosts should be able to open a \"Manage occurrences\" dialog from a recurring booking and confirm or reject individual pending occurrences without affecting the statuses of other bookings in the series.\n\nExisting bulk confirmation actions should remain available.\n\n### Acceptance Criteria\n\n- [ ] **AC1:** Recurring booking rows in the Unconfirmed and Recurring tabs provide a \"Manage occurrences\" action that opens a dialog listing all occurrences with their date, time, and current status, ordered chronologically.\n- [ ] **AC2:** Each eligible pending occurrence has its own Confirm and Reject actions.\n- [ ] **AC3:** Confirming an individual occurrence updates only that booking to ACCEPTED. All other occurrence statuses remain unchanged.\n- [ ] **AC4:** Rejecting an individual occurrence uses the existing rejection-reason dialog, saves the reason, and updates only that booking to REJECTED.\n- [ ] **AC5:** Past, confirmed, rejected, and canceled occurrences do not display individual Confirm or Reject actions. The backend also rejects invalid individual confirmation or rejection requests.\n- [ ] **AC6:** Existing \"Confirm all\" and \"Reject all\" actions remain functional and continue operating on pending bookings according to the current bulk workflow.\n- [ ] **AC7:** After an individual action, the dialog and Bookings dashboard refresh to display the updated statuses and pending booking count.\n- [ ] **AC8:** Only authorized hosts can retrieve and manage occurrences belonging to their bookings.\n- [ ] **AC9:** Automated tests verify individual confirmation, individual rejection, invalid status handling, authorization, and preservation of unrelated occurrence statuses.\n- [ ] **AC10:** New interface text uses the existing internationalization system.\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Changing how attendees create recurring bookings.\n- Modifying recurrence frequency or scheduling rules.\n- Redesigning the entire Bookings dashboard.\n- Replacing existing bulk confirmation actions.\n- Adding new attendee notification templates.\n- Changing payment or refund policies.\n- Changing calendar integration behavior beyond what is required to prevent regressions.\n\n### Scope Estimate: Medium\n\nThe backend already supports individual booking confirmation and rejection, reducing the amount of new business logic required.\n\nThe main implementation work involves:\n\n- Adding a query to retrieve all occurrences in a recurring series, including booking IDs and statuses.\n- Creating a Manage occurrences dialog.\n- Reusing existing confirmation and rejection functionality.\n- Strengthening backend validation for individual actions.\n- Adding frontend and backend tests.\n\n\n### Decision\n\nImplement a **Manage occurrences dialog** accessible from recurring booking rows in the Unconfirmed and Recurring tabs.\n\nThe dialog will retrieve the individual bookings in a series and display their dates, statuses, and available confirmation actions.\n\nExisting confirmation handlers and UI components will be reused wherever possible.\n\n### Alternatives Considered\n\n**Alternative A: Expand the recurring booking row**\n\nAdd an expandable list directly beneath each recurring booking, with Confirm and Reject actions for every occurrence.\n\nAdvantages:\n- Allows hosts to manage dates directly from the booking list.\n- Reuses existing confirmation components.\n\nDisadvantages:\n- Could make the Bookings table cluttered for long recurring series.\n- Requires additional changes to the existing booking row layout.\n- May introduce more UI confirmation.\n\nAdvantages:\n- Could reuse existing booking details components.\n- Avoids introducing another management interface.\n\nDisadvantages:\n- The existing details sheet is behind the Rationale\n\nAlternative B provides the best balance of usability, implementation scope, and code reuse.\n\nThe dialog keeps recurring bookings grouped in the dashboard while allowing hosts to manage individual dates. Issue #139 (CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy, assigned to Julissa): stop attendees from cancelling within N minutes of the start; hosts can always cancel.

**PR 1 (UI only), implemented 2026-11-12 on branch `feat/issue-139-min-cancellation-notice-ui`, branched from `team/main` with no upstream set. Not committed yet; Julissa commits herself, see [[feedback_no-autonomous-commits]].**
- Adds `MinimumCancellationNoticeController.tsx` in the Advanced tab folder:
  - a props-controlled `MinimumCancellationNoticeController`;
  - a default-export `MinimumCancellationNoticeSetting` wrapper that is hidden unless the `minimum-cancellation-notice` flag is on, also hides while `disabledCancelling` is on, and keeps the value in local state, never in the form.
- Also adds the flag to `config.ts` and `useFlags.ts`, an `OPERATIONAL` seed migration `20261112120000_…` set to off (matching repo convention), and 4 `common.json` keys.
- The `EventAdvancedTab` test harness now wraps everything in `FeatureProvider` and has a placement test. 22 tests in total. Checks were rerun 2026-11-12 with only the stale-tRPC `BookerWebWrapper` error remaining.
- Chose "at least N minutes" wording: cancelling exactly at the boundary is allowed.

**Update 2026-11-16 (supersedes the earlier 2a/2b/2c split and the "enforce in both places + requestedAt" plan below):** Julissa wants exactly 2 PRs. The revised PR-2 spec (in chat, not approved yet) works like this:
- **Enforce only in `/api/cancel`, before the task is queued.** The decision is made when the attendee asks, so the 5-minute delay doesn't matter. API v2 is out of scope, and the other `handleCancelBooking` callers (reportBooking, CalendarSyncService) are host actions.
- **Recurring series: the check is required, not optional.** The email cancel link sends `allRemainingBookings` (`CalEventParser.ts:113`), and `handleCancelBooking` cancels every occurrence with start ≥ now. So check the earliest active occurrence, reusing `getActiveRecurringBookingsFromDate` and `findBookingByUidWithEventType`.
- **Gate the `?cancel=true` deep link** too, since that's the default email path.
- **Identify hosts by the session user being `booking.userId`.**
- **The feature flag gates only the UI.**
- **Size:** about 19 files (~12 code files). That's over the 10-file guideline, but justified as mostly 1-line wiring forced by the type system.
- **PR #142's body says "Fixes #139",** which would auto-close the issue when it merges. Suggest changing it to "Part of #139".

**PR 2 (backend), not started. Plan:**
- Add a `minimumCancellationNotice Int?` column. Remember the managed-props map at `zod-utils.ts` `allManagedEventTypeProps`, which requires every column.
- Enforce in both `/api/cancel/route.ts`, before the 5-minute soft-cancel task is queued, and `handleCancelBooking`.
- Pass `requestedAt` in the task payload.
- Identify hosts by session userId only. The `cancelledBy` email can be spoofed through the URL.
- Write a new helper, because the reschedule helper returns false once the event has started.
- Gate the `?cancel=true` deep link on the booking page.

**Why:** Sprint 3 check-in needed a small, safe slice; the backend has blockers.

**How to apply:** In PR 2, swap the wrapper's local state for a form Controller on `minimumCancellationNotice`; the controller component is reused unchanged.

**D6 mutation testing setup, done 2026-11-19 (nothing committed):**
- Lives on the local-only branch `test/issue-139-mutation`, cut from the PR #142 branch.
- The shared Stryker files were copied from Zach Bowden's PR #140; the shared config originally came from Zachary Short's #135. #142 and #140 share the same base, so the copy is exact.
- Added `stryker.139.config.mjs` and `vitest.stryker-139.config.mts`. The scope is the whole Controller file, `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:843-843` and `useFlags.ts:28-28`, which Julissa chose to keep.
- Windows: Stryker 10 needs Node 22. Node 22.23.5 is installed next to Node 20, which stays the default. Her nvm (Author Software v2) has no `exec`, so call `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Author Software\nvm\installs\v22.23.5\node.exe node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/bin/stryker.js run stryker.139.config.mjs`.
- Verified with a dry run: 51 mutants, 22 tests pass.
- Resume steps and credits are in `docs/sprint3/mutation/139-julissaehp-setup.md`, which is uncommitted.
- Next: after PR 2, move the files onto the PR 2 branch, add the backend ranges and tests, then do the official before/after runs.

**PR 2 backend (#150), implemented 2026-11-19, uncommitted, awaiting Julissa's review:**
- Branch `feat/issue-150-min-cancellation-notice-backend` in the main checkout, cut from team/main `1ca2a73` with no upstream. A temporary worktree `../cal.diy-issue-150` was created and then removed while clean.
- Stryker setup was moved off the working tree first:
  - The tracked part is in the stash named "issue-139 D6 Stryker setup (tracked)…": package.json/yarn.lock Stryker deps, .gitignore, and unformatted regenerated app-store `*.generated.ts`.
  - A full file backup, including all untracked files, is at `../backups/2026-11-19-issue-139-stryker-setup/`.
  - The untracked Stryker configs and docs stay in the working tree.
  - To resume: `git checkout test/issue-139-mutation && git stash apply <that stash>`.
- Design (supersedes the plans above):
  - Enforce only in `/api/cancel`, before the tasker. The pure logic is in `packages/features/bookings/lib/minimumCancellationNotice.ts`.
  - The host check mirrors the booking page's `checkIfUserIsHost` (organizer, or an event-type host who is an attendee), using the session only.
  - The window stays active after the start (unlike the reschedule helper).
  - For recurring `allRemainingBookings`, the earliest active occurrence ≥ now decides.
  - The flag gates the settings UI only.
  - Returns 403 with an English message.
- Integration gap: #142's wrapper still uses useState. Swapping it to the `minimumCancellationNotice` form field (~10 lines) has to happen in whichever PR merges second.
- Checks: 66 new/touched tests pass, apps/web tsc reports 0 errors, and Biome has no new diagnostics vs team/main.
- The PR description draft is in `../pr-drafts/issue-150-backend-pr.md`.

# Issue #139 mutation testing: setup notes (pre-D6)

**not** the D6 deliverable. The deliverable will be `139-julissaehp.md` with the before and after reports in
`reports/`. Fold the "Setup notes" and "Credits" sections below into it when it is written.

  `cc4ae59fd5`). Nothing is committed or pushed.

  - `stryker.config.mjs`

  changes. Their diff hashes the same as #140's.

| From | What I reused |

A per-issue `vitest.stryker-<N>.config.mts` with an explicit `include` list. Running Node 22 next to a default Node 20. The D6 write-up template. |

## Windows-specific setup

1. **Node 22 next to Node 20.**
   - Stryker 10.1.1 declares `engines.node >=22.0.0`, and this machine's default Node is 20.20.2.
   - Install it with `nvm install 22`. This installed 22.23.5, and the default stays 20.20.2. Do **not** run `nvm use 22`.
   - This nvm (Author Software nvm v2.0.0) has no `nvm exec`, so Bowden's `nvm exec 22 …` does not work here.
   - Instead, call Node 22's `node.exe` by its full path:
     `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Author Software\nvm\installs\v22.23.5\node.exe`
2. **Run Stryker's JS entry point directly.** Use `node_modules/@stryker-mutator/core/bin/stryker.js`, because
   `node_modules/.bin/stryker` is a shell shim that would pick up the default Node 20.
3. **Install without build scripts.** `yarn install --mode=skip-build` added the 98 Stryker packages and left
   `yarn.lock` unchanged. It also skips the root postinstall, which would regenerate Prisma and app-store files and
   could overwrite uncommitted work.
4. **Set `TZ=UTC` in PowerShell** with `$env:TZ="UTC"`. In Git Bash, a `TZ=UTC` prefix works.
5. **Symlinks.** `CLAUDE.md` (pointing to `AGENTS.md`) is a real symlink here (`core.symlinks=true`). The sandbox copy
   handled it, so no extra ignore pattern was needed. If a future run fails while copying a symlink, add its path to
   `ignorePatterns` in `stryker.139.config.mjs` only.
6. **The progress reporter is downgraded.** Stryker reports that the console does not support `progress` and switches
   to `progress-append-only`. This is harmless.

508	+# Mutation testing: Issue #138 -- Allow hosts to confirm or reject individual recurring booking occurrences
509	+
510	+**PR(s):** [#140](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/140)  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner  **Config:** [stryker.138.config.mjs](../../../stryker.138.config.mjs) + [vitest.stryker-138.config.mts](../../../vitest.stryker-138.config.mts), built on the shared [stryker.config.mjs](../../../stryker.config.mjs) by @zach-short  **Command:** `STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/138-zachbowden-<before|after>.json TZ=UTC nvm exec 22 node_modules/.bin/stryker run stryker.138.config.mjs`
511	+**Reports:** [before](reports/138-zachbowden-before.json) · [after](reports/138-zachbowden-after.json)
512	+**Mutation score:** before 50.60% → after 81.71% (covered mutants only: 73.68% → 97.10%)
513	+
514	+### Setup notes
515	+
516	+- **Only the lines this PR added or changed are mutated.** `stryker.138.config.mjs` lists them as line ranges: the new guard in `confirm.handler.ts`, `findByRecurringEventId` in `BookingRepository.ts`, the new lines in `BookingListItem.tsx`, and all of `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx` and the two `getRecurringOccurrences` files.
517	+- **The test list is explicit.** `vitest.stryker-138.config.mts` names this PR's test files plus `BookingRepository.test.ts`. The shared config's `related: true` would also run every test that imports `BookingRepository`, including unrelated calendar-subscription suites that time out under load. A failure on the unmutated code stops Stryker before it mutates anything.
518	+- **Stryker 10 requires Node 22 or newer;** the machine's default is Node 20, so the run uses `nvm exec 22`.
519	+- **Same mutants in both runs.** Both runs produced 99 mutants at identical locations, so the reports compare one-to-one.
520	+
521	+| Status | Before | After |
522	+|---|---|---|
523	+| Killed | 42 | 67 |
524	+| Survived | 15 | 2 |
525	+| No coverage | 26 | 13 |
526	+| Ignored (static) | 16 | 17 |
527	+
528	+## Surviving mutants
529	+
530	+All 15 survivors from the before report are in lines this PR added.
531	+
532	+| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
533	+|---|---|---|---|
534	+| `confirm.handler.ts:187` | `if (!recurringEventId)` → `if (true)` | Test gap (killed after) | The new pending/not-ended guard is meant only for single-booking requests. No test sent a bulk request whose first booking fails the guard, so applying it to bulk requests went unnoticed. Under the mutant, "Confirm all" on a series whose first booking has ended would be refused. The issue (Q2) says the bulk behaviour must not change. |
535	+| `confirm.handler.ts:191` | status error message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Tests checked only `code: "BAD_REQUEST"`. API v2 and email-link callers get this message as their only explanation. The project's error-handling rule requires errors that name the record and the reason. |
536	+| `confirm.handler.ts:194` | `endTime < now` → `endTime <= now` | Equivalent | Only differs when the booking ends at exactly the current millisecond. The AC says "past" without defining that instant, and no test can reliably create that state. |
537	+| `confirm.handler.ts:197` | "already ended" message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Same as line 191. |
538	+| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:23` | FORBIDDEN message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Only the error code was asserted. |
539	+| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:29` | `booking?.recurringEventId` → `booking.recurringEventId` | Test gap (killed after) | No test for a booking id that does not exist. Under the mutant, the query throws a `TypeError` (shown as a 500 error) instead of `BAD_REQUEST`. |
540	+| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:32` | "not part of a recurring series" message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Only the error code was asserted. |
541	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:42` | query input `{ bookingId }` → `{}` | Test gap (killed after) | The tRPC mock ignored its arguments, so nothing checked that the dialog asks for this booking's series (AC1, AC8). |
542	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:43` | `{ enabled: isOpenDialog }` → `{}` | Test gap (killed after) | Nothing checked that the query waits until the dialog is open. Under the mutant, every recurring row on the page would fetch its series on load. |
543	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:51` | title → empty | Test gap (killed after) | No test asserted the dialog title (AC1, AC10). |
544	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:52` | description → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Same as line 51. |
545	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:60` | `occurrences?.map` → `occurrences.map` | Test gap (killed after) | The tests always supplied data. If the query errors (no data, not loading), the mutant crashes the dialog. |
546	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:63` | `endTime >= now` → `endTime > now` | Equivalent | Same millisecond boundary as `confirm.handler.ts:194`, on the UI side. |
547	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:74` | date format `"ddd, D MMM YYYY"` → `""` | Test gap (killed after) | AC1 requires the date. Tests used relative dates and only checked status badges, so a wrong date format went unnoticed. |
548	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:77` | `{" "}` in the time range → `""` | Test gap (killed after) | AC1 requires the time. No test checked the rendered time text, so "10:00am -10:15am" would have passed. |
549	+
550	+**Mutants with no coverage** (not survivors, but they count against the score):
551	+- **`BookingRepository.ts:685-689`, `findByRecurringEventId` (11 mutants).** The handler test mocks the repository, so the method never ran in any test. A new repository test killed all 11.
552	+- **`ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:57`, loading text.** No test rendered the loading state. Killed after.
553	+- **`getRecurringOccurrences.schema.ts:7`, the Zod schema.** No test imported it. The new schema test runs it, but the schema is built when the module first loads, and `ignoreStatic` is on (from the shared config), so the after report lists it as **Ignored** rather than Killed. The new test still checks the schema rejects `{}`, `1.5` and `"5"`.
554	+- **`BookingListItem.tsx:171-172`, `473-483` (13 mutants), still uncovered.** These lines decide when to show the "Manage occurrences" button and open the dialog. No unit test renders a booking row, because the row needs the data-table, actions-store and details-sheet providers. AC1's button placement was checked manually (see PR #140's Test Evidence), but this is still a gap in the automated tests.
555	+
556	+## New or strengthened test
557	+
558	+Commit: [PR #140](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/140/files) · Test: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.individual.test.ts` › keeps Confirm all working when the series' first booking has already ended · Kills: `confirm.handler.ts:187` (`if (true)`)
559	+
560	+The same change added or strengthened these tests, each killing the mutants listed (all show as Killed in the after report):
561	+

563	+|---|---|
564	+| `confirm.handler.individual.test.ts` › refuses to act on a REJECTED / CANCELLED occurrence; refuses to act on an occurrence that has already ended (now also assert the message names the booking and the reason) | `confirm.handler.ts:191`, `:197` |
565	+| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.test.ts` › throws BAD_REQUEST when the booking does not exist | `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:29` |
566	+| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.test.ts` › FORBIDDEN and not-recurring cases now also assert the message | `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:23`, `:32` |
567	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › fetches this booking's series only while the dialog is open | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:42`, `:43` |
568	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows the translated title and description | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:51`, `:52` |
569	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows no rows when the query returns no data | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:60` |
570	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows each occurrence's date and time in the host's time zone and time format | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:74`, `:77` |
571	+| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows a loading message while the occurrences load | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:57` (was no coverage) |
572	+| `BookingRepository.test.ts` › findByRecurringEventId returns the series' occurrences in chronological order with only the fields needed to act on them | `BookingRepository.ts:685-689` (11, were no coverage) |
573	+| `getRecurringOccurrences.schema.test.ts` (new) | `getRecurringOccurrences.schema.ts:7` (now Ignored as static, see above) |
574	+
575	+## Questions
576	+
577	+**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**
578	+
579	+My tests checked actions, not what the user or caller sees. The handler tests asserted the error code but never the message, which is all an API v2 or email-link caller gets. The dialog tests checked which buttons appear and what they send, but never the date and time AC1 requires, nor the title. Because those tests used dates relative to "now", they could not have asserted a formatted date anyway. The survivors also showed I had only tested the happy path. Nothing covered a booking that doesn't exist, a query with no data, or a bulk request whose first booking is in the past. That last one mattered most. My new guard was meant for single-booking requests, but no test would have caught it also blocking "Confirm all", which the issue says must not change. Finally, the 11 uncovered `BookingRepository` mutants showed that mocking the repository in the handler test meant the real query never ran in any test.
580	+
581	+**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**
582	+
583	+Not directly: the survivors came from missing assertions, not wrong expected values. They did force me to decide where some expected values come from. The ACs don't specify error wording, so the new message assertions don't copy the strings from the code. They only require that the message names the booking id and the reason (its status, or that it ended), which comes from the project's documented error-handling rule. For the date/time test, I worked out "Wed, 4 Mar 2099" and "10:00am - 10:15am" for 15:00 UTC in New York independently of the component. The date format matches the one the booking list already uses. The two boundary mutants (`<` vs `<=`, `>=` vs `>`) are the opposite case. The AC says "past" but doesn't define the exact ending instant, so no requirement gives an expected value. That's why I classified them as equivalent rather than adding a test pinned to my own choice.
584	+
585	+**3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**
586	+
587	+I used Claude Code (log linked from PR #140).
588	+
589	+- **Configuration:** it applied @zach-short's shared Stryker setup and wrote the issue-specific config. It mutates only this PR's changed line ranges and lists the test files explicitly, because `related: true` would also pull in calendar-subscription tests that time out.
590	+- **Running:** the first run failed because Stryker 10 requires Node 22 and my machine had Node 20; I installed Node 22 with nvm and ran Stryker through it.
591	+- **Analysis and tests:** it drafted the classification of the 15 survivors and the new tests.
592	+- **What I verified:**
593	+  - All 6 selected test files (36 tests) pass before mutation.
594	+  - The before and after reports contain the same 99 mutants at the same locations.
595	+  - Each "test gap" survivor shows as Killed in the after report.
596	+  - The computed scores match Stryker's own summary table (81.71% / 97.10%).
597	+- **What I corrected:** its first estimate counted the schema mutant as killed, but the after report shows it as Ignored (a static mutant with `ignoreStatic` on). This write-up reports it that way.

import { useMemo } from "react";

import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { useLocale } from "@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale";

import type {
  RowData,
  BookingRowData,
  BookingListingStatus,
  BookingOutput,
  BookingsGetOutput,
} from "../types";

/**
 * Transform raw bookings into final data structure with separators
 * - Deduplicates recurring bookings for recurring/unconfirmed/cancelled tabs
 * - For "upcoming" status, organizes into "Today" and "Next" sections
 */
export function useBookingListData({
  data,
  status,
  userTimeZone,
}: {
  data?: BookingsGetOutput;
  status: BookingListingStatus;
  userTimeZone?: string;
}) {
  const { t } = useLocale();

  // Build a Map for recurringInfo lookups
  const recurringInfoMap = useMemo(() => {
    const map = new Map<string, NonNullable<typeof data>["recurringInfo"][number]>();
    for (const info of data?.recurringInfo ?? []) {
      if (info.recurringEventId) {
        map.set(info.recurringEventId, info);
      }
    }
    return map;
  }, [data?.recurringInfo]);

  /**
   * Transform raw bookings into flat list (excluding today's bookings for "upcoming" status)
   * - Deduplicates recurring bookings for recurring/unconfirmed/cancelled tabs
   * - For "upcoming" status, filters out today's bookings (they're shown in separate "Today" section)
   */
  const flatData = useMemo<BookingRowData[]>(() => {
    const todayDateString = dayjs().tz(userTimeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD");

    // For recurring/unconfirmed/cancelled tabs: track recurring series to show only one representative booking per series
    // Key: recurringEventId, Value: array of all bookings in that series
    const shownBookings: Record<string, BookingOutput[]> = {};

    const filterBookings = (booking: BookingOutput) => {
      // Deduplicate recurring bookings for specific status tabs
      // This ensures we show only ONE booking per recurring series instead of all occurrences
      if (status === "recurring" || status == "unconfirmed" || status === "cancelled") {
        // Non-recurring bookings are always shown
        if (!booking.recurringEventId) {
          return true;
        }

        // If we've already encountered this recurring series
        if (
          shownBookings[booking.recurringEventId] !== undefined &&
          shownBookings[booking.recurringEventId].length > 0
        ) {
          // Store this occurrence but DON'T display it (return false to filter out)
          shownBookings[booking.recurringEventId].push(booking);
          return false;
        }

        // First occurrence of this recurring series - show it and start tracking
        shownBookings[booking.recurringEventId] = [booking];
      } else if (status === "upcoming") {
        // For "upcoming" tab, exclude today's bookings (they're shown separately in the "Today" section)
        return dayjs(booking.startTime).tz(userTimeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD") !== todayDateString;
      }
      return true;
    };

    return (
      data?.bookings.filter(filterBookings).map((booking) => ({
        type: "data" as const,
        booking,
        recurringInfo: booking.recurringEventId ? recurringInfoMap.get(booking.recurringEventId) : undefined,
        isToday: false,
      })) || []
    );
  }, [data?.bookings, recurringInfoMap, status, userTimeZone]);

  // Extract today's bookings for the "Today" section (only used in "upcoming" status)
  const bookingsToday = useMemo<BookingRowData[]>(() => {
    const todayDateString = dayjs().tz(userTimeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD");

    return (data?.bookings ?? [])
      .filter(
        (booking: BookingOutput) =>
          dayjs(booking.startTime).tz(userTimeZone).format("YYYY-MM-DD") === todayDateString
      )
      .map((booking) => ({
        type: "data" as const,
        booking,
        recurringInfo: booking.recurringEventId ? recurringInfoMap.get(booking.recurringEventId) : undefined,
        isToday: true,
      }));
  }, [data?.bookings, recurringInfoMap, userTimeZone]);

  // Combine data with section separators for "upcoming" tab
  const finalData = useMemo<RowData[]>(() => {
    // For other statuses, just return the flat list
    if (status !== "upcoming") {
      return flatData;
    }

    // For "upcoming" status, organize into "Today" and "Next" sections
    const merged: RowData[] = [];
    if (bookingsToday.length > 0) {
      merged.push({ type: "separator" as const, label: t("today") }, ...bookingsToday);
    }
    if (flatData.length > 0) {

function addStatusesQueryFilters(query: BookingsUnionQuery, statuses: InputByStatus[]) {
  if (statuses?.length) {
    return query.where(({ eb, or, and }) =>
      or(
        statuses.map((status) => {
          if (status === "upcoming") {
            return and([
              eb("Booking.endTime", ">=", new Date()),
              or([
                and([eb("Booking.recurringEventId", "is not", null), eb("Booking.status", "=", "accepted")]),
                and([
                  eb("Booking.recurringEventId", "is", null),
                  eb("Booking.status", "not in", ["cancelled", "rejected"]),
                ]),
              ]),
            ]);
          }

          if (status === "recurring") {
            return and([
              eb("Booking.endTime", ">=", new Date()),
              eb("Booking.recurringEventId", "is not", null),
              eb("Booking.status", "not in", ["cancelled", "rejected"]),
            ]);
          }

          if (status === "past") {
            return and([
              eb("Booking.endTime", "<=", new Date()),
              eb("Booking.status", "not in", ["cancelled", "rejected"]),
            ]);
          }

          if (status === "cancelled") {
            return eb("Booking.status", "in", ["cancelled", "rejected"]);
          }

          if (status === "unconfirmed") {
            return and([eb("Booking.endTime", ">=", new Date()), eb("Booking.status", "=", "pending")]);
          }
          return and([]);
        })
      )
    );
  }

  return query;
}

async function handler(request: NextRequest) {
  const searchParams = request.nextUrl.searchParams;

  const { action, token, reason } = querySchema.parse(Object.fromEntries(searchParams.entries()));

  const decryptedData = JSON.parse(
    symmetricDecrypt(decodeURIComponent(token), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")
  );

  const {
    bookingUid,
    userId,
    platformClientId,
    platformRescheduleUrl,
    platformCancelUrl,
    platformBookingUrl,
  } = decryptedSchema.parse(decryptedData);

  const booking = await prisma.booking.findUniqueOrThrow({
    where: { uid: bookingUid },
  });

  const user = await prisma.user.findUniqueOrThrow({
    where: { id: userId },
    select: {
      id: true,
      uuid: true,
      email: true,
      username: true,
      role: true,
      destinationCalendar: true,
    },
  });

  try {
    await confirmHandler({
      ctx: {
        user: {
          id: user.id,
          uuid: user.uuid,
          email: user.email,
          username: user.username ?? "",
          role: user.role,
          destinationCalendar: user.destinationCalendar ?? null,
        },
        traceContext: distributedTracing.createTrace("confirm_booking_magic_link"),
      },
      input: {
        bookingId: booking.id,
        recurringEventId: booking.recurringEventId || undefined,
        confirmed: action === DirectAction.ACCEPT,
        reason,
        emailsEnabled: true,
        platformClientParams: platformClientId
          ? {
              platformClientId,
              platformRescheduleUrl,
              platformCancelUrl,
              platformBookingUrl,
            }
          : undefined,
      },
    });
  } catch (e) {
    let message = "Error confirming booking";
    if (e instanceof TRPCError) message = (e as TRPCError).message;
    return NextResponse.redirect(
      new URL(`/booking/${bookingUid}?error=${encodeURIComponent(message)}`, WEBAPP_URL)
    );
  }

  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL(`/booking/${bookingUid}`, WEBAPP_URL));
}

export const GET = defaultResponderForAppDir(handler);

  async confirmBooking(bookingUid: string, requestUser: ApiAuthGuardUser) {
    const booking = await this.bookingsRepository.getByUid(bookingUid);
    if (!booking) {
      throw new NotFoundException(`Booking with uid=${bookingUid} was not found in the database`);
    }

    const platformClientParams = booking.eventTypeId
      ? await this.platformBookingsService.getOAuthClientParams(booking.eventTypeId)
      : undefined;

    const emailsEnabled = platformClientParams ? platformClientParams.arePlatformEmailsEnabled : true;
    const userCalendars = await this.usersRepository.findByIdWithCalendars(requestUser.id);

    await confirmBookingHandler({
      ctx: {
        user: {
          ...requestUser,

        confirmed: true,
        recurringEventId: booking.recurringEventId ?? undefined,
        emailsEnabled,
        platformClientParams,
        actionSource: "API_V2",
        actor: makeUserActor(requestUser.uuid),
      },
    });

    return this.getBooking(bookingUid, requestUser);
  }

  async declineBooking(bookingUid: string, requestUser: ApiAuthGuardUser, reason?: string) {

      : undefined;

OPEN
### What does this PR do?

Adds a shared StrykerJS setup for the Sprint 3 mutation testing deliverable (D6), so each of us can run the tool on the files our own PRs change. No product code changes. There is no issue for this yet; it is team tooling for D6.

### What changed

- `package.json` / `yarn.lock`: `@stryker-mutator/core` and `@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner` 10.1.1 as root dev dependencies. 10.1.1 supports our Vitest 4.1.8 and needs Node 22 or later.
- `stryker.config.mjs`: Vitest runner with the root `vitest.config.mts`, `related: true` (only tests that import the mutated file run), clear-text, progress, JSON and HTML reporters. The JSON report goes to `STRYKER_JSON` if set.
- `.gitignore`: ignores the local `reports/mutation/` output and `.stryker-tmp/`.

### How to use it

Run it only on the files your PR changed:

```bash
TZ=UTC STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json yarn stryker run --mutate "path/to/changed-file.ts"
```

Then add or strengthen a test, and run again with `-after.json`. Commit both JSON reports with your D6 write-up. If you use this setup, credit it in your D6 file as the course asks.

### Design decisions

**Sandbox vs in-place.** I tried `inPlace: true` first, because the default sandbox copies the repo. In this monorepo the in-place backup lands inside the project, Vitest then collected the backup copies, and the restore dropped the executable bit on three tracked scripts. The sandbox avoids both, at the cost of a copy. The copy leaves out `docs`, `ai-logs`, `specs`, `apps/api/v2`, `apps/web/public`, `packages/embeds` and `reports` to stay small, and `.claude`, `.cursor` and `packages/prisma/.env`, because they are symlinks the copy cannot follow.

**Related tests only vs a fixed test folder.** `vitest.related` runs the tests that import the mutated file. A fixed `vitest.dir` per run would need each of us to pick the folder and risks false survivors when a covering test sits elsewhere.

### Tech Debt

* **Introduced:** Stryker's sandbox copy adds a few seconds per run. The ignore list must grow if someone adds another symlinked folder.
* **Encountered:** On Node 26, `yarn prisma generate` exits with code 1 (the Zod generator uses a removed `fs` option while it deletes old output), although it still writes every file. This also makes the root `postinstall` fail on Node 26.

### Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stryker runs on one file with only its related tests | Manual: `TZ=UTC yarn stryker run --mutate packages/features/auth/lib/identityProviders.ts` → initial run 8 tests passed; 2 mutants tested, 2 killed; done in 7 s | manual | StrykerJS docs |
| Stryker runs on a React component with jsdom tests | Manual: `--mutate apps/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes.tsx` → initial run 14 tests passed; 62 killed, 122 survived, 138 no coverage (score 19.25%); done in 35 s | manual | StrykerJS docs |
| A run leaves no change in tracked files | Manual: `git status --short` after both runs shows no tracked changes | manual | course D6 (commit only the reports) |

**Not tested automatically, and why:** this PR adds tooling, not product behavior; the checks above are the tool's own runs.

**AI-written tests:** None.

I can't reproduce these sections verbatim because the full text exceeds the 125-character limit on quotes from source documents. Below is a condensed version of each requirement, with short quoted phrases where exact wording matters.

## D2 - Requirements Specification (20 pts, individual)
- Use the same format and requirements as Sprint 1 D2.
- Write and review specs before coding starts.
- The review is a comment on the issue stating what the reviewer checked: whether each acceptance criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered and whether they are covered, and whether the scope fits.
- If the reviewer finds problems, they list them and the author updates the spec. A bare "Looks good!" is not acceptable.
- Bug fixes use a bug format (observed and expected behavior, reproduction steps, other details). Other hardening or feature work uses a short task format (problem, goal, acceptance criteria, necessary details).

## D3 - Design Decisions (5 pts, individual)
- Same as Sprint 2 D3: each decision names at least two concrete alternatives and explains the choice.
- Each issue needs at least one non-trivial decision.

## D4 - Code Changes and Pull Requests (20 pts, individual)
**Workflow:** Same as Sprint 2 D4, including the Tech Debt section.

**Test Evidence section:** Every PR description includes one. It replaces the "how it was tested" part of the description.
- **Table columns:** Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value.
- **Rows:** One per acceptance criterion from D2. For bug reports, use the Expected Behavior instead. For PRs that change no product behavior (such as CI changes), write "N/A" and explain why.
- **Test(s):** Give the test name and file if not obvious. For manual checks, write "Manual:" followed by the steps and what you observed. If an AC is tested both ways, list both.
- **Level:** `unit`, `integration`, `E2E`, or `manual`.
- **Source of expected value:** `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`, `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain). The current output of your own code is not a valid source.
- **Not tested automatically, and why:** Only for ACs checked manually.
- **AI-written tests:** List any tests written or modified by AI and how you checked their expected values. Write "None" if none.
- AI may draft this section, but you are responsible for its accuracy.
- If your fork has no CI, list the commands you ran and a summary of the results (passed, failed, skipped).
- Reviewers add a rubric line for test evidence, scored 1–10, with notes.

**Review and merge rules:**
- Merge only after a teammate approves the **latest commit**. Merging without approval, or after pushing new commits since approval, is not allowed.
- The author may merge once approved.
- Request review on GitHub and notify the reviewer on Zulip. Reviewers respond within 24 hours.
- Each code PR links its issue with `Closes #<issue>` and is attached to the `Sprint 3` milestone.
- Open a code PR by the Nov 12 check-in.

The page does not give PR size limits; refer to Sprints 1 and 2 for those.

**Grading (per PR, aggregated and normalized to 20):**

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| Change implements the D2 acceptance criteria | 6 |
| Tests appropriate; Test Evidence complete, with every AC covered and expected values justified | 6 |
| Description explains what and why; Tech Debt section present; issue linked | 3 |
| CI passes (or manual verification documented) | 3 |
| Reviewed with the rubric, reviewer comment posted, merged only after approval on latest commit | 2 |

## D5 - AI Logs (5 pts, individual)
- Same requirements as Sprint 1 D5 and the AI Log Instructions page.
- **Real logs only:** They must show your prompts and the AI's output. SpecStory format is recommended.
- **Not accepted:** Session summaries, paraphrased prompts, share links, or tool output without the prompts that produced it.
- **File name:** `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`
- **Location:** `ai-logs/sprint3/<your-github-username>/`
- Link each log from the issue or PR it documents.
- Check your setup against the AI Log Instructions before your first session.

## D6 - Mutation Testing (15 pts, individual; new in Sprint 3)
This replaces the Sprint 2 UML diagrams.

**Scope:**
- Choose one of your issues whose PR changes both source code and tests. CSCI 535 students must do two such issues; the small issue may be one of them.
- Run the tool only on the source files changed by that PR, not the whole project.

**Steps:**
1. Run the tool and analyze every surviving mutant as either equivalent (no test can kill it) or a test gap. If there are more than 10 survivors, analyze at least 10, starting with lines your PR added or changed.
2. Add or strengthen at least one test that kills a survivor revealing a gap, then re-run the tool to confirm. If no survivor reveals a gap, say so and justify it in the survivors table.
3. Answer the template's questions.

**Tool (required; manual mutation does not count):**

| Stack | Tool |
|---|---|
| TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest | StrykerJS with the Vitest runner |
| TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa) | StrykerJS with the Jest runner |
| Go (Gitea backend) | Gremlins or go-mutesting |

**Configuration and credit:**
- Each student configures and runs the tool on their own files and commits the configuration used.
- You may reuse a teammate's setup, but you must run the tool yourself and credit the teammate in your report.

**Reports and file locations:**
- Enable machine-readable output: add `"json"` to StrykerJS `reporters`, use `--output=<file>.json` with Gremlins, or save go-mutesting terminal output to a text file.
- Commit the first-run and re-run reports to `docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/` as `<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and `-after.json` (`.txt` for go-mutesting).
- Reported scores must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as killed in the "after" report.

**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`, containing:
- Header: issue title, PR(s), tool, config link (with teammate credit if reused), command, before/after report links, and mutation score before and after.
- **Surviving mutants table:** Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why.
- **New or strengthened test:** commit link, test name, and the mutant it kills.
- **Questions:**
  1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
  2. Did any survivor point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.
  3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct? Otherwise write "N/A."

**Common problems the page lists:** the run stops if selected tests fail on unchanged code; tests running against built output rather than source; required services not running; false survivors from limiting tests (for example, with Vitest's `dir` option); long run times.

**If blocked:** Ask teammates first, then contact the TA early with the errors and your AI log. The TA may approve a different issue or code area. Problems reported at the end of the sprint do not excuse a missing D6.

**Rubric:**

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| Tool run on PR files; config, command, results, and reports committed | 4 |
| Survivors analyzed correctly (equivalent vs. gap, with explanation) | 4 |
| At least one test kills a survivor; re-run confirms | 4 |
| Answers show understanding, not just description | 3 |

For CSCI 535, the D6 score is the average of the two submissions.

## Submission Checklist
Push everything to your team repository by **Nov 19, 11:59 PM**, except the check-in, which is due **Nov 12**:
- Sprint 3 milestone with all selected issues attached, assigned, and scoped (D1)
- Issue bodies with stories or bug reports, acceptance criteria, design decisions, and spec review comments (D2, D3)
- All PRs merged after approval on the latest commit, each with issue link, Tech Debt and Test Evidence sections, and a posted review rubric (D4)
- AI logs in `ai-logs/sprint3/<username>/`, correctly named and linked (D5)
- Mutation write-ups and before/after reports in `docs/sprint3/mutation/` (two of each for CSCI 535) (D6)
- Check-in at `docs/sprint3/checkin/<username>.md` linking an open or merged code PR, due Nov 12 (D7)
- Sprint report at `docs/sprint3/report.md` (or .pdf/.docx), including the suite health section (D8)
- Sprint 3 release tag and GitHub release, created after the last merge (D9)
- Individual D10 reflection survey submitted

# Review of PR #140: confirm or reject individual recurring occurrences (issue #138)

**Recommendation: Request Changes.** The core feature is well built, and the code and tests are better than average for our team. But one change in behaviour that the issue told us to test before finishing (Risk 1) is real and untested. There are also a few small Sprint 3 deliverable gaps.

PR head reviewed: `5c43345`. Nothing was posted to GitHub, and your branch, working tree, stash and Stryker files were not touched.

## What I checked myself vs. what the author reported

**Ran myself**, in a throwaway clone of the PR head that I deleted afterwards:
- The PR's 6 test files: **36 passed**.
- The related existing suites (booking, dialog, magic-link, verify-token, BookingRepository, `viewer/bookings`): **15 files passed, 2 skipped; 178 tests passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed.** This matches the author's report; their counts were lower only because tests were added later.
- **Probe A** (scratch only, not in the PR): ran the real `confirmHandler` on Confirm all. Confirmed the calendar recurrence it builds (finding B1).
- **Probe B** (scratch only): ran the real `useBookingListData`. Confirmed that a row's representative booking changes after an individual action (finding M1).
- **Mutation reports:** recomputed from both JSON files. Before 50.60% (73.68% of covered mutants), after 81.71% (97.10%). The same 99 mutants at the same locations in both runs, and no production code changed between the two runs. All of this matches the write-up.

**Author's claims I did not verify:**
- Type check (`apps/web` tsc, 0 errors). I didn't re-run it because it needs the tRPC types rebuilt for the new procedure.
- Biome.
- The manual UI checks.

**CI:** the "Prepare" check fails on every fork PR (#142 too) during dependency installation, so that failure isn't caused by this PR.

## 1. Acceptance criteria

| AC | Status | Evidence / gap |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 Manage occurrences: a dialog listing every occurrence in time order | **Satisfied** | Repository `orderBy startTime asc`; dialog tests. Button placement is checked only by hand (13 mutants with no coverage). |
| AC2 Confirm/Reject on each eligible occurrence | **Satisfied** | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:62-63`, plus a test |
| AC3 Confirming one occurrence changes only that booking | **Satisfied** | Single-booking path: `handleConfirmation`'s non-recurring branch updates only `bookingId`. The tests mock that branch, so the evidence is indirect. |
| AC4 Reject uses the reason dialog, saves the reason, changes only that booking | **Satisfied** | The test drives the real `RejectionReasonDialog`; the handler test asserts the update |
| AC5 No actions on past or non-pending occurrences; backend refuses them | **Satisfied** | `confirm.handler.ts:185-200`. It's a read-then-write check, so it doesn't stop two simultaneous requests (L2). |
| AC6 Confirm all / Reject all still work | **Partially** | Unchanged on an all-pending series. **Wrong calendar results after individual actions (B1).** |
| AC7 Dialog and dashboard refresh | **Partially** | Invalidation is correct. **The dialog closes after acting on the row's own booking (M1).** |
| AC8 Only authorized hosts | **Satisfied** | Access checked on the requested booking; `recurringEventId` is read on the server; confirm re-checks each booking |
| AC9 Automated tests | **Satisfied (unit level)** | "Other occurrences unchanged" is shown only by `updateMany`/`findMany` never being called, with Prisma mocked |
| AC10 i18n | **Satisfied** | 3 keys added, no duplicates, valid JSON |

From a host's point of view, the feature works for "act on some dates and leave the rest". It breaks down when the host then clicks Confirm all, or acts on the date their row is showing.

## 2. Findings

### BLOCKER

**B1. Confirm all after individual actions writes wrong events to calendars** (violates AC6 and the issue's "prevent regressions" scope)

- **Where:** `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:350-363`
  ```ts
  const groupedRecurringBookings = await prisma.booking.groupBy({
    where: { recurringEventId: booking.recurringEventId }, // no status filter
  ...
  recurringEvent.count = groupedRecurringBookings[0]._count;
  ```
- **How it fails:**
  - `handleConfirmation.ts:81` creates one calendar event, starting at the clicked row's booking, with `count` = every booking in the series of any status.
  - Google writes that count into the event's repeat rule (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:218-222`).
  - Before this PR, a series was always fully pending when Confirm all ran, so the count was right. This PR's UI makes mixed series normal.
- **Scenario:** a 4-week series. The host confirms week 1 and rejects week 3 in the dialog, then clicks Confirm all on the Unconfirmed row, which now represents week 2. The calendar gets a series of 4 starting at week 2: week 2, week 3 (rejected), week 4, and a **phantom week 5**. Week 1 already has its own event. If the host had confirmed week 3 instead, it would be **duplicated**.
- **Verified:** by reading the code, plus Probe A (`groupBy` has no status filter; the event gets `count: 4` and week 2's start time). I didn't test against a live calendar.
- **Why it's a blocker:**
  - Issue Risk 1 said this "should be tested before implementation is finalized", and spec review item 4 asked for a test or a manual step.
  - The PR lists it under Tech Debt as "possible" and hands the manual check to reviewers without a result.
  - It puts wrong dates into attendees' calendars.
- **Possible fixes** (the author should choose):
  - Hide Confirm all and Reject all once any occurrence is no longer pending.
  - Or confirm a mixed series one booking at a time instead of as one repeating event.
  - Or at minimum, run the manual check and add a test.

### HIGH

None besides B1.

### MEDIUM

**M1. The dialog closes when the host acts on the row's own occurrence** (partially violates AC7)

- **Where:**
  - `apps/web/components/booking/BookingListItem.tsx:172` keeps the dialog's open/closed state inside the row.
  - `apps/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useBookingListColumns.tsx:133` renders the row with `key={booking.id}`.
- **How it fails:**
  - In the Unconfirmed tab, the row is the series' first pending booking, which is also the first date with buttons in the dialog.
  - Acting on it makes the next pending booking the row's booking. The new `key` makes the row remount, and the dialog closes.
  - In the Recurring tab, the same thing happens when the host rejects the first date.
- **Verified:** Probe B confirmed the row's booking switches from #1 to #2. React remounting on a key change is standard behaviour. I didn't check it in a browser.
- **Fix:** lift the dialog state up, or key it by `recurringEventId`.

**M2. Sprint 3 D4/D5 gaps**
- The PR has **no Sprint 3 milestone** (the issue does). D4 requires one.
- The AI log is real, correctly named and in the right folder, but it **isn't linked** from the PR or the issue, as D5 requires. The D6 write-up says "log linked from PR #140". The draft PR body in the log had an "AI Log" section, but it was dropped from the posted body.

### LOW

- **L1. Two mutants are misclassified** (`confirm.handler.ts:194` `<`→`<=`, `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:63` `>=`→`>`). They aren't equivalent: behaviour differs when `endTime === now`, and `vi.setSystemTime` makes that easy to test. A more accurate label is "unspecified boundary". The UI and backend do agree on the boundary, so a consistency test would be justified.
- **L2. Simultaneous requests.** The new check reads the status and then writes with `update where {id}` instead of a conditional update. Confirm plus reject, or an individual confirm racing Confirm all, can both pass the check, giving duplicate events or emails, or a booking that is REJECTED but still on the calendar. This race already existed and the PR makes it narrower. It's theoretical: it needs two tabs, two admins, or the email link plus the dialog.
- **L3. Representative-occurrence access.** The whole series is returned after checking access to one booking. A rescheduled occurrence keeps the `recurringEventId` (`createBooking.ts:249-250`) and could belong to another host, so its id, uid, time and status would be shown. Round-robin co-hosts already have access to each other's bookings through `isUserAHost`, so this only matters in edge cases. Confirming is still checked per booking. Theoretical.
- **L4. No error state in the dialog.** If the query fails, `isPending` is false and `data` is undefined, so the dialog shows an empty list with no message. The button also doesn't check whether the viewer is the host, so a user who isn't would see an empty dialog. Needs testing.
- **L5. Recurring-tab row loses Confirm all.** After the host confirms the earliest date, the Recurring-tab row now represents an accepted booking. `shouldShowPendingActions` therefore hides Confirm all and Reject all, even though later dates are still pending. Workaround: use the Unconfirmed tab.
- **L6. `BookingListItem.tsx:171` puts the visibility check inline**, unlike the existing `shouldShow*` helpers in `bookingActions.ts`, which have unit tests. Moving it there would cover the 13 mutants with no coverage, and AC1's button placement would no longer depend on a manual check.
- **L7. Scope.**
  - The PR includes #135's shared Stryker setup (deps, lockfile, `stryker.config.mjs`) and a stray root `.gitkeep`.
  - It changes about 20 non-doc files, more than the repo's 10-file guideline. The spec review had suggested a 2-PR split.
  - The Test Evidence is out of date: it says "21 new tests in 4 new files", but there are 5 new test files.

## 3. Architecture and security summary

- **Good:**
  - Reuses `AcceptBookingButton`, `RejectBookingButton`, `useBookingConfirmation` and `BookingAccessService`.
  - Uses `select` in Prisma.
  - The repository method follows the naming rules.
  - The new check sits after the access check, so it doesn't reveal status to unauthorized users.
  - The new query only runs while the dialog is open.
- **Design decision 2 is right.** Before this PR, a REJECTED or CANCELLED single booking could be "confirmed". Email links and API v2 send `recurringEventId` for recurring bookings, so only non-recurring callers see the new 400. The PR documents that change.
- **Small debts, already listed by the author:** reusing `findByIdForReassignmentValidation`, and the handler using Prisma directly.

## 4. Deliverables

- **D2:** the spec review is substantive.

```markdown
Thanks for this — the dialog is clean, it reuses the existing buttons/hook/access service well, and the new single-booking guard closes a real hole (REJECTED/CANCELLED bookings could previously be "confirmed"). I checked out `5c43345` in a scratch clone and ran the 6 PR test files (36 passed) plus the related booking/dialog/link suites (178 passed, 9 skipped). I also recomputed the D6 numbers from both JSON reports: 99 identical mutants, 50.60% → 81.71%, matching your write-up.

**Must fix before merge**
1. **Confirm all after individual actions (AC6, issue Risk 1).** `confirm.handler.ts:350-363` sets the calendar `recurringEvent.count` from a `groupBy` over *all* statuses, starting at the clicked row's booking. Example: 4 weekly dates, confirm wk1 and reject wk3 in the dialog, then Confirm all from the Unconfirmed row (now wk2) → one recurring event of 4 starting wk2: includes the rejected wk3 and a phantom wk5 (and duplicates any date confirmed individually after the start). I confirmed the count/start with a handler-level probe; not tried against a live calendar. The issue asked for this to be tested before finalizing — could you either prevent bulk actions once a series is mixed, or confirm mixed series per-occurrence, and add a test?
2. **Dialog closes after acting on the row's own occurrence (AC7).** Rows are keyed `key={booking.id}` (`useBookingListColumns.tsx:133`) and the open state lives in `BookingListItem`. In the Unconfirmed tab the row's booking is the first pending date — acting on it promotes the next one, the row remounts and the dialog closes (same for reject in the Recurring tab). Lifting the state or keying by `recurringEventId` would fix it.
3. **Sprint 3 items:** attach the PR to the Sprint 3 milestone, and link the AI log from the PR/issue (the D6 doc says it's linked, but the PR body doesn't have it).

**Smaller notes**
- D6: the two boundary survivors aren't truly equivalent — `vi.setSystemTime` can create `endTime === now`. Maybe call them "unspecified boundary" or add a test that pins UI/backend consistency.
- Moving `canManageOccurrences` into `bookingActions.ts` as a `shouldShow*` helper would cover the 13 no-coverage mutants and AC1's placement without the full row providers.
- The dialog shows an empty list on query error (no error state).
- The check-then-update guard doesn't stop concurrent confirm/reject (pre-existing race, just narrower now).
- The PR carries #135's Stryker setup and a root `.gitkeep`; Test Evidence still says "21 new tests in 4 new files".

+import { ManageOccurrencesDialog } from "@calcom/web/components/dialog/ManageOccurrencesDialog";
+import { useEffect } from "react";
+
+import { useManageOccurrencesStore } from "../store/manageOccurrencesStore";
+
+export function ManageOccurrencesDialogHost({
+  userTimeZone,
+  userTimeFormat,
+}: {
+  userTimeZone?: string;
+  userTimeFormat?: number | null;
+}) {
+  const bookingId = useManageOccurrencesStore((state) => state.bookingId);
+  const setBookingId = useManageOccurrencesStore((state) => state.setBookingId);
+
+  // The store is global, so close the dialog when the bookings list goes away.
+  useEffect(() => () => setBookingId(null), [setBookingId]);
+
+  if (bookingId === null) return null;
+
+  return (
+    <ManageOccurrencesDialog
+      isOpenDialog
+      setIsOpenDialog={(open) => {
+        if (!open) setBookingId(null);
+      }}
+      bookingId={bookingId}
+      userTimeZone={userTimeZone}
+      userTimeFormat={userTimeFormat}
+    />
+  );
+}

+import { create } from "zustand";

+  bookingId: null,
+  setBookingId: (bookingId) => set({ bookingId }),
+}));

7:Hosts could only **Confirm all** or **Reject all** dates in a recurring series from the Bookings dashboard. The backend could already handle one booking at a time, but the UI gave no way to do it. This PR adds a **Manage occurrences** dialog where a host confirms or rejects single dates and leaves the rest of the series unchanged.
17:- **`ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx`** (new): lists each occurrence with its date, time range (in the host's time zone and time format) and a status badge. Only upcoming `PENDING` occurrences get Reject and Confirm buttons. These are the existing `RejectBookingButton` and `AcceptBookingButton` with no recurring flags, so they send single-booking requests, and Reject opens the existing `RejectionReasonDialog`.
23:### 1. Where hosts manage individual occurrences
29:- **Rationale:** (a) clutters the table for long series and changes the row layout, which raises regression risk. (b) sits behind the `bookings-v3` feature flag, so most hosts would not see it. A dialog leaves the list unchanged and has room for dates, statuses and actions.
30:- **Consequences:** Small, self-contained UI change that is easy to test on its own. It costs the host one extra click.
39:- **Consequences:** Email links and API v2 now get a 400 when they try to confirm or reject a past, rejected or cancelled single booking. This is a behaviour change for non-recurring bookings too, but the UI already hid these actions. The bulk path is untouched, so AC6 is preserved.
55:- **Rationale:** With the recurring flags left out, `useBookingConfirmation` already sends a single-booking request (no `recurringEventId`), uses the existing rejection-reason dialog (AC4), and invalidates `viewer.bookings.*` and `bookingUnconfirmedCount` on success (AC7). No new mutation code was needed.
74:| **AC4:** Rejecting one occurrence uses the rejection-reason dialog, saves the reason, sets only that booking to REJECTED | `confirm.handler.individual.test.ts` › rejects only the requested occurrence and stores the reason<br>`ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › rejects a single occurrence through the rejection reason dialog | unit | AC |
76:| **AC6:** Confirm all and Reject all still work on pending bookings as before | `confirm.handler.individual.test.ts` › keeps Confirm all passing the series id to the bulk confirmation flow · keeps bulk reject limited to pending occurrences of the series<br>`useBookingConfirmation.test.tsx` › keeps Confirm all sending the series id (Recurring tab, Unconfirmed tab) | unit | AC, upstream behavior |
77:| **AC7:** After an individual action, the dialog and dashboard refresh statuses and the pending count | `useBookingConfirmation.test.tsx` › refreshes bookings (including the occurrences list) and the unconfirmed count after ACCEPTED / REJECTED | unit | AC |
78:| **AC8:** Only authorized hosts can retrieve and manage occurrences of their bookings | `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.test.ts` › throws FORBIDDEN and does not read the series when the user has no access<br>`confirm.handler.individual.test.ts` › refuses unauthorized users before revealing the booking status | unit | AC, issue discussion (spec review: reuse `BookingAccessService`) |
79:| **AC9:** Automated tests cover individual confirm, individual reject, invalid status, authorization, and preservation of other statuses | All tests listed above (21 new tests in 4 new files) | unit | AC |
83:- **AC1 (button placement):** the button in `BookingListItem` needs the full booking-list providers (data table, actions store, details-sheet store) to render, so its placement was checked by hand.
84:- **AC7 (actual re-render):** the test checks that `viewer.bookings.*` (which includes the new `getRecurringOccurrences` query) and `bookingUnconfirmedCount` are invalidated. The re-fetch after invalidation is React Query behaviour, which these tests mock.
85:- **AC6 (calendar side of Confirm all):** `handleConfirmation` and the calendar integrations are mocked. This PR does not change them, and the existing `confirm.handler.test.ts` that exercised them is entirely `describe.skip`.
88:- **Expected values come from the issue, not the code's output.** Each assertion was written from the AC text and the spec-review comment before the tests were run. For example: only an upcoming `PENDING` booking may be acted on, a reject stores exactly the reason given, an unauthorized user gets `UNAUTHORIZED`/`FORBIDDEN` before any status check, and bulk reject only touches `PENDING` bookings.

Every occurrence in a series normally has the same organizer, and `confirmHandler` still checks access per booking, but the occurrence list itself is not filtered per booking.
129:- **Reused a repository method with a use-case-specific name.** The new handler calls `BookingRepository.findByIdForReassignmentValidation` to read `recurringEventId`, rather than adding a near-duplicate method. A generic name (e.g. `findByIdIncludeStatusAndRecurringEventId`) would be cleaner.

import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { ManageOccurrencesDialogHost } from "./ManageOccurrencesDialogHost";

  mockConfirm: vi.fn(),
  mockUseQuery: vi.fn(),

}));

  trpc: {
    useUtils: () => ({
      viewer: { bookings: { invalidate: vi.fn() }, me: { bookingUnconfirmedCount: { invalidate: vi.fn() } } },
    }),
    viewer: {
      bookings: {
        getRecurringOccurrences: {
          useQuery: (input: unknown, options: unknown) => {
            mockUseQuery(input, options);
            return occurrencesQuery;
          },
        },
        confirm: { useMutation: () => ({ mutate: mockConfirm, isPending: false }) },
      },
    },
  },
}));

// The controlled Dialog calls useRouter, which throws outside a mounted Next.js app router.
vi.mock("next/navigation", async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import("next/navigation")>();
  return { ...actual, useRouter: vi.fn(() => ({ push: vi.fn() })) };
});

vi.mock("@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale", () => ({
  useLocale: () => ({ t: (key: string) => key, i18n: { language: "en" } }),
}));

const inTwoDays = new Date(Date.now() + 48 * 3600_000);
const occurrence = (status: BookingStatus) => ({
  id: 3,
  uid: "uid-3",
  status,
  startTime: inTwoDays,
  endTime: new Date(inTwoDays.getTime() + 3600_000),
});

const openFor = (bookingId: number | null) =>
  act(() => useManageOccurrencesStore.getState().setBookingId(bookingId));

describe("ManageOccurrencesDialogHost", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    openFor(null);
    occurrencesQuery.data = [occurrence(BookingStatus.PENDING)];
  });

  it("renders nothing until a series is chosen", () => {
    render(<ManageOccurrencesDialogHost userTimeZone="UTC" />);

    expect(screen.queryByTestId("manage-occurrences-dialog")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("opens the dialog for the booking chosen from the list", () => {
    render(<ManageOccurrencesDialogHost userTimeZone="UTC" />);

    openFor(7);

    expect(screen.getByTestId("manage-occurrences-dialog")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(mockUseQuery).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ bookingId: 7 }, { enabled: true });
  });

  it("stays open with the refreshed statuses after a date is confirmed", () => {
    const { rerender } = render(<ManageOccurrencesDialogHost userTimeZone="UTC" />);
    openFor(7);

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("confirm"));
    expect(mockConfirm).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ bookingId: 3, confirmed: true, reason: "" });

    occurrencesQuery.data = [occurrence(BookingStatus.ACCEPTED)];
    rerender(<ManageOccurrencesDialogHost userTimeZone="UTC" />);

    expect(screen.getByTestId("manage-occurrences-dialog")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText("confirmed")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(mockUseQuery).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith({ bookingId: 7 }, { enabled: true });
  });

  it("forgets the chosen series when the dialog is closed", () => {
    render(<ManageOccurrencesDialogHost userTimeZone="UTC" />);
    openFor(7);

    fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("dialog-rejection"));

    expect(useManageOccurrencesStore.getState().bookingId).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByTestId("manage-occurrences-dialog")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("forgets the chosen series when the bookings list unmounts", () => {
    const { unmount } = render(<ManageOccurrencesDialogHost userTimeZone="UTC" />);
    openFor(7);

    unmount();

    expect(useManageOccurrencesStore.getState().bookingId).toBeNull();
  });
});

         if (occurrences.some((occurrence) => occurrence.status !== BookingStatus.PENDING)) {

           }
           return { message: "Booking confirmed", status: BookingStatus.ACCEPTED };
         }
       }
